title: Party Competition: An Agent-Based Model

key_points.claim: Laver & Sergenti present a book-length ABM treatment of multiparty electoral competition (political domain of artificial societies).
key_points.evidence_quote: the first comprehensive treatment of party competition using the computational techniques of agent-based modeling

key_points.claim: Model treats party competition as a dynamic process with entry/exit of parties and adaptive agents with imperfect information.
key_points.evidence_quote: political parties rise and fall... must constantly adapt their behavior to yesterday’s political outcomes

key_points.claim: Finding: satisficing party decision rules outperform relentless vote-maximizing search.
key_points.evidence_quote: politicians who are satisfied with relatively modest vote shares often do better at winning votes than rivals who search ceaselessly

key_points.claim: Finding: parties weighting leaders' own preferences can do better than purely voter-responsive ones; valence advantages matter.
key_points.evidence_quote: politicians who pay close attention to their personal preferences when setting party policy often have more success

key_points.claim: Voters are heterogeneous with preferences over many issues; politics framed as a complex non-equilibrium system.
key_points.evidence_quote: politics is best viewed as a complex dynamical system that is neither random nor in equilibrium

reliability_notes: Publisher's catalog page (abstract/blurb and endorsements only; no full text). Abstract only. Claims are the publisher's summary of results, not verified; no model details or figures.
